scope: Audit of the current HSConfig repository implementation on branch codex/no-silent-default-only-closure at commit eb411b4cb15c9df668ea8fd4e7ac29df8b6b1840. The audit covers supported atomic claim kinds, source_contract_matrix policy rows, source_claim_lifecycle, source_claim_conflicts, surface gate decisions, builder/router lowering, source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, surface_status_ledger, contract_spine_sentinel, output ownership, report ownership, and operator_summary as the only normal apply authority.
verified_strengths: The audited branch was verified in C:/Users/darbo/Documents/HSConfig as codex/no-silent-default-only-closure with HEAD eb411b4cb15c9df668ea8fd4e7ac29df8b6b1840.

The atomic source vocabulary is explicit and finite: archetype, mulligan_keep, mulligan_discard, card_role, targeting_rule, combo_sequence, gameplan_posture, hero_power_transform, mechanic_usage, known_bad_pattern, tech_slot, replacement_option, discover_choice, choose_one_choice, and globalvalue_numeric_tuning.
source_contract_matrix has a policy row for every supported claim kind and fails closed on missing or extra policy/detail rows.

The policy matrix separates report_only rows from runtime_lowerable, suppressed_or_conditional, and runtime_evidence_required rows; globalvalue_numeric_tuning is intentionally runtime-evidence-required and not Step1 lowerable.

Surface gates enforce claim-kind-specific runtime authority: Mulligan only accepts mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard, Combo accepts combo_sequence, GlobalValues accepts gameplan_posture overlays, and CardID behavior accepts card behavior claim families under identity and semantic requirements.
Start-of-game, deck, and hero-power-transform effects are explicitly blocked from becoming Mulligan keeps unless the source states opening-hand Mulligan intent.

source_claim_lifecycle centralizes claim normalization, claim_id assignment, policy lane attachment, conflict quarantine, runtime eligibility, and surface-specific gate decisions before builders or routers emit runtime rows.
source_claim_conflicts downgrades conflicting claims to report-visible quarantines instead of silently choosing a winner.
Builders and routers consume lifecycle-filtered claims rather than raw source claims, preserving claim IDs, surface gate reasons, and suppression reasons in downstream reports.

Mulligan, CardID, Combo, and GlobalValues builders preserve the no-silent-default-only policy by distinguishing source-backed, policy-backed, static-semantics-backed, suppressed, and default-only outcomes.

source_contract_audit records claim lifecycle rows with surface gate decision, builder/router decision, runtime surface, emitted files, first missing link, final runtime effect, and diagnostic-only operator impact.
source_to_runtime_explainability projects audit rows into operator-facing missing-link and next-source-action diagnostics while declaring authority=diagnostic_only and apply_blocking=false.

operator_summary now carries surface_status_ledger rows for runtime surfaces, including status, default_only, first_missing_link, next_source_action, runtime_permission_impact=none, and operator_impact=diagnostic_only.

Default-only surfaces are visible in operator_summary through default_only_runtime_surfaces, default_only_runtime_surface_details, no_default_only_verdict, and surface_status_ledger, while remaining nonblocking for load-safe apply.

contract_spine_sentinel currently reports status=clean, no policy/spine claim-kind drift, no diagnostic apply consumers, no lifecycle gate files, no unclassified outputs, no forbidden legacy surfaces, and reports/operator_summary.json as the only report ownership gate.

evaluate_apply_gate and runtime_apply re-evaluate reports/operator_summary.json and package structure instead of consuming source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, source_contract_conformance, claim_lifecycle_rows, or contract_spine_rows.

Report ownership and output ownership classify operator_summary as the normal operator gate, classify source-contract/explainability reports as diagnostic, and keep Presume.json and Concede.json outside the normal runtime output path.
correctness_gaps: No confirmed hard apply-authority correctness break was found in the audited implementation.

Combo surface gating can approve combo_sequence as the correct surface while the combo builder still suppresses incomplete sequences such as sequence_too_short; tests treat this as an expected builder prerequisite gap, so diagnostics must keep separating gate eligibility from builder completeness.

CardID card_role claims can be visible without becoming meaningful runtime behavior unless an explicit behavior change is present; audit and explainability consumers must keep distinguishing report/static visibility from emitted runtime effect.

GlobalValues can be load-safe with only baseline/static coverage even when no source-backed changed keys exist; this is correct as load safety but must stay visible as configuration richness debt rather than hidden success.

Legacy claim_type normalization is still accepted at ingestion; the lifecycle layer currently migrates it to claim_kind, but future code should avoid using claim_type as an independent contract surface.

The design relies on coordinated updates across policy rows, surface gates, builder expectations, conformance rows, docs, and sentinel tests when adding a claim kind; missing one layer would be contract drift, although current sentinel coverage is designed to catch it.
default_only_gaps: Default-only surfaces are intentionally warnings, not apply blockers; a package can be runtime-load-safe while strategically thin, so operators must inspect default_only_runtime_surface_details and source_to_runtime_explainability when the ledger reports default_only.

surface_status_ledger is embedded in operator_summary rather than a separate artifact; packages generated before this schema can lack the compact ledger even though operator_summary remains the apply authority.

Policy-backed autonomous Mulligan can prevent a Mulligan surface from being default-only, but it is still weaker than source-backed guide evidence; the policy_backed versus source_backed distinction must remain visible.

CardID behavior and Combo are not minimal load-safe requirements, so absence of rich source-backed rows on those surfaces can remain a diagnostic or richness issue rather than a technical apply block.
The no_default_only_verdict has runtime_permission_impact=none by design; future UI or automation must not mistake a visible_warning for a runtime apply denial.
slimness_gaps: The repository now has several adjacent diagnostic views: source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, source_claim_gap_report, source_contract_conformance, contract_spine_sentinel, output_ownership_manifest, and report_ownership. They are controlled, but future additions should avoid creating duplicate authority surfaces.

surface_status_ledger derives from config usefulness and source-to-runtime explainability inside operator_summary; adding a parallel ledger file would increase cognitive load unless it answers a distinct operator need.

Policy rows, conformance expectations, docs, and tests duplicate some contract facts intentionally for drift detection; this is useful guardrail duplication but increases the cost of adding a new claim family.

The legacy allow_source_informed parameter remains as a backward-compatible no-op. This is acceptable now, but the codebase should keep sentinel coverage around it so the flag cannot regain gate meaning.

Operator summary is doing both gate ownership and diagnostic presentation. This is acceptable because the gate fields remain explicit, but future expansions should keep diagnostic sections compact and non-authoritative.
autonomy_gaps: Strict surface gates make HSConfig safe but conservative: unsupported, underspecified, or identity-ambiguous source claims become report-visible instead of generated runtime behavior.
Discover and choose-one claims require exact option identity before CardID behavior can lower them, so unresolved option identity limits autonomous richness.
globalvalue_numeric_tuning requires runtime evidence outside the pre-run HSConfig scope, so the repository cannot autonomously tune raw GlobalValues numbers from guide prose alone.
Conflict quarantine prevents false lowering but can suppress otherwise useful runtime rows until the source conflict is repaired.

Full source-backed coverage depends on upstream source extraction providing claim_kind, CardID identity, semantic qualifiers, and required fields; the runtime spine does not invent missing source evidence.

Default-only and static-semantics-backed packages can still be valid for apply, so operator autonomy relies on the ledger and diagnostic reports to prioritize source improvement rather than automatic blocking.
guardrails_to_keep: Keep reports/operator_summary.json as the only normal apply authority.

Keep evaluate_apply_gate and runtime_apply independent from source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, source_contract_conformance, claim_lifecycle_rows, contract_spine_rows, and surface_status_ledger.
Keep every source-contract diagnostic marked authority=diagnostic_only or operator_gate_impact=diagnostic_only with apply_blocking=false.
Keep source claims lowering only through surface-specific gate functions and lifecycle-filtered builder/router inputs.
Keep start-of-game, deck, and hero-power-transform effects out of Mulligan keeps unless opening-hand Mulligan intent is explicit.
Keep globalvalue_numeric_tuning blocked until runtime evidence and never Step1-lowerable from guide text alone.
Keep conflict quarantine before builder/router lowering so contradictions stay report-visible and cannot silently emit runtime rows.
Keep Presume.json and Concede.json forbidden in the normal runtime output surface.
Keep report_ownership and output_ownership sentinel checks so exactly one gate file exists and every output is classified.
Keep policy-backed autonomous Mulligan explicit and visible as policy_backed, not source_backed.
Keep HSConfig inside its pre-run deck-to-config scope with no replay parsing, winrate validation, candidate promotion, or post-run tuning.
recommended_next_design: Retain the current contract spine with surface ledger. The best next design is subtractive and coverage-focused: keep the chain source claim -> lifecycle/conflict quarantine -> surface gate -> builder/router -> runtime effect, keep source_contract_audit and source_to_runtime_explainability diagnostic-only, keep surface_status_ledger as the compact operator view inside operator_summary, and preserve reports/operator_summary.json plus evaluate_apply_gate/runtime_apply as the only normal apply authority. Future claim kinds or runtime surfaces should be added only with full policy rows, gate logic, builder/router behavior, conformance snapshot coverage, sentinel checks, output/report ownership, docs, and tests. Improve source evidence and identity resolution before adding heuristic runtime fallbacks or a second gate.
